name: The Dropout – Who Is Elizabeth Holmes?
summary:
Who is Elizabeth Holmes? With a new film out, the disgraced Theranos founder chronicled in "The Dropout" sparks controversy again.

The new film "You Can See Everything" has put Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced Theranos founder, back in the spotlight. But what really happened? From the podcast "The Dropout" and interviews with former Theranos whistleblowers and patients to going behind the scenes of the fictionalized Hulu series starring Amanda Seyfried, ABC News has chronicled every step of the saga surrounding Holmes. The college dropout-turned-tech entrepreneur charmed Silicon Valley, claiming her company would change the world with just a few drops of blood. Instead, a jury found her guilty of fraud. She was sentenced to prison but continues to profess her innocence. "IMPACT x Nightline" brings the microscope to the Silicon Valley scandal that captured the world's attention.

name: How far can Jordan Love take the Packers?, Are the Bears the most complete team in the NFC??
summary:
First Take begins as the Packers put a beat down on the Panthers last night. Jordan Love put together another great game to help the Packers keep pace with the rest of the NFC North. Could this Packers team be a contender in the NFC once Micah Parsons returns? Next the opening week rivalry between Luka Doncic and Yaxel Lendeborg gets it's second chapter as the Lakers travel to take on the Warriors tonight. Will we see sparks fly once again? Then Chris Canty, co-host of UnSportsmanLike on ESPN2, and Dan Orlovsky debate who would be harder to tackle, Derrick Henry or Bijan Robinson. 

First Take resumes as the Bears take on the Seahawks on Monday night in what could be an NFC Championship game preview. How will newcomers Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons impact this game? Next the crew breaks down some early NBA overreactions. Are the Heat already finished? Are OKC's title hopes gone without JDub and Cason Wallace? Then the crew goes over some of the best teams in the NFL that might have something haunting over them. Chiefs offense, Bills defense, Vikings offense; which of these teams can overcome their haunting horrors?

Here you'll find a posh gated community with winding tree-lined streets and luxurious mansions to call home. At the center of this community are the Duprees, a powerful and prestigious multi-generational family that is the very definition of Black royalty. But behind these pristine walls and lush, manicured gardens are juicy secrets and scandals waiting to be uncovered. And those that live outside these gates are watching closely. show.name: Mystery Science Theater 3000
show.summary:
Mystery Science Theater 3000 started as a locally produced television show for KTMA in Minnesota but soon grew in popularity. It moved to Comedy Central (originally the Comedy Channel), then to Syfy. After an eighteen-year hiatus, the crew of the Satellite of Love returned in 2017, airing on Netflix for two seasons. In 2021, the production started its own streaming service, The Gizmoplex, where the riffing of cheesy movies continues. Rifftrax revitalised the series once again in 2026 with four more episodes of the series. 

Over the years, there have been several "test subjects": Joel Robinson, Mike Nelson, Jonah Heston, and Emily Connor along with their robot friends Tom Servo, Crow T Robot, and Gypsy (now GPC) all subjected to bad movies thanks to a host of mad scientists including Doctor Clayton Forrester, his mother Pearl, and most recently Kinga Forrester.

name: Justice for Faith
summary:
On Sept. 7, 2012, UNC Chapel Hill sophomore Faith Hedgepeth was found murdered in her off-campus apartment, leaving her family and friends devastated and desperate for answers. Who would want to kill her? A devoted member of the Haliwa-Saponi tribe, Faith was known for her outgoing personality and vibrant social life. Thousands of potential suspects were investigated, and hundreds of DNA samples were tested, but despite the involvement of the FBI, state agencies and private investigators, the case remained unsolved for years. In 2016, there was a break in the case. Investigators turned to DNA phenotyping technology, with Parabon Nano Labs generating a composite sketch of a potential suspect whose ancestry was described as Native American and European or Latino. Still, years passed without an arrest. Then, in 2021, authorities announced a major breakthrough: Miguel Enrique Salguero-Olivares had been arrested in connection with Faith's murder after DNA collected during a DUI stop matched evidence from the crime scene. Although he had no known personal connection to Faith, he was reportedly working near her apartment around the time of her death. 

Following the jury's recent announcement of a guilty verdict against Salguero-Olivares, "20/20" correspondent Ryan Smith examines the murder of Faith Hedgepeth, the yearslong investigation that led to the arrest, and the DNA evidence that helped bring the case to trial. With the verdict just announced, the all-new report revisits the search for answers in a case that haunted Faith's loved ones for more than 13 years.
